artifacts.rights_basis: The work was first published in New York in 1889, before 1929, so it is in the United States public domain by publication date. The Project Gutenberg wrapper -- its licence, its trademark references and its marker lines -- is excluded from this file by the stated transformation, so nothing Project Gutenberg authored survives in these bytes and Triptych claims no exclusive right in the source wording. THE FILE ITSELF NAMES NO PRINTING: its Project Gutenberg header gives only a title, an author, a translator or editor where there is one, a release date and a language, so the first-publication fact above is the work's, carried on this work's own record, and not a statement about which printing was transcribed. That is enough to settle the rights question and not enough to identify an edition, which is why the edition record claims none.

This file is wrapped in Project Gutenberg's licence header and footer, which carry the Project Gutenberg trademark and conditions on its use. The wrapper-bearing bytes are therefore recorded as the hashed derivation input and are not retained in Git; what is retained is the derivative named in `notes`, from which the wrapper has been removed, leaving only the text whose rights the permission page settles.
